messages.subject: line transect selection
parts:
I am trying to develop protocals for estimating abundance and =
distribution of juvenile chinook salmon in the Lower American River. I =
want to compare density estimates among habitat types(i.e. =
riffle,run,glyde,pool), but am not sure how to properly choose line =
transect distances or locations. =20

One general design I was considering was to randomly select a starting =
river mile location (the entire river segment I am interested in is 23 =
miles long) and have 3 dive crews(2 divers in each crew) sample a 0.5 =
mile stretch on a given day. The sampling would occur bi-weekly and a =
new river mile starting location would be chosen at random each day of =
sampling. The three dive crews would be distributed as follows: 1 crew =
close to the right bank, 1 at midchannel, and 1 at the left bank. The =
crews would simultaneously start sampling in an upstream direction. In =
this design a particular transect could and probably will cross habitat =
types. Will this present a problem for comparing density among habitat =
types? Should my line transects only incorporate one habitat type?

If my sample size is low for a particular transect can I pool transects =
from similar habitat types? =20

Are there alternative designs worth considering that will allow =
comparisons of density among habitat types to be made?

Thank you
